titre: Child support and your tax return
resume: The paying parent can deduct child support, the receiving parent declares it. With shared residence, no deduction but the tax shares are split. What to keep as proof.
aQuoiCaSert: Child support paid for a child counts in the income tax of both parents: it is deducted by one and added to the taxable income of the other. It never appears on the pre-filled tax return: each parent must enter it themselves. Declaring it correctly, with proof, avoids errors and tax reassessments.
quiEstConcerne: The parent who pays support for a minor child who lives with the other parent.
The parent who receives the support.
The parent raising their children alone (box T).
aSavoir: Paying parent, minor child: the support is deductible if the child does not usually live with you and is not your dependent for tax purposes. With a court judgment, you deduct the amount set (as indexed), plus expenses paid directly (canteen, schooling, medical costs). Costs related to visiting rights are not deductible.
Support without a judgment: the amount must match the child's needs and your means, and you must be able to prove the payments.

Receiving parent: the support is taxable, up to what the other parent can deduct. It is declared under "Pensions, retraites, rentes", line "Pensions alimentaires perçues". A 10% allowance is applied automatically.
Shared residence: no support is deductible. Each parent counts 1/4 share for each of the first two children, then 1/2 share per child from the third.

Box T: a single, divorced or separated parent living alone with their dependent children ticks box T and gets an extra half share (1/4 share for one child in shared residence, 1/2 share for two or more).

Adult child not attached to your tax household and not living with you: proven expenses are deductible up to €6,855 per child (current scale according to service-public.gouv.fr); the child declares the amount received themselves.

documents.libelle: Judgment or agreement setting the support (copy)
documents.detail: Ask the court registry (greffe), the lawyer or the notary for a copy if you no longer have it.

documents.libelle: Proof of each payment during the year
documents.detail: Bank statements, transfer notices, ARIPA certificate if the support is paid through the Caf (Caisse d'allocations familiales, the family benefits office). Cash without a receipt is hard to prove.

documents.libelle: Invoices for expenses paid directly for the child
documents.detail: School canteen, schooling, medical costs, if you deduct them on top of the support.

documents.libelle: Annual summary of amounts paid or received
documents.detail: Total for the calendar year. You can export it from the Lien Parental Journal.
Download it from your personal account on impots.gouv.fr.

documents.libelle: Decision or agreement setting the residence (shared or not)
documents.detail: To justify the split of shares or box T if the tax authorities ask.

etapes.titre: Add up the amounts paid or received over the calendar year
etapes.detail: The Journal (Finances filter, Pension category) gives you the history of recorded payments.

etapes.titre: Check before filling in your tax return
etapes.detail: The total matches your bank statements; the child is not declared as your dependent if you deduct the support; with shared residence you deduct nothing; the proof is stored in the Vault.
As deductible expenses if you pay it, under "Pensions alimentaires perçues" if you receive it. It is never pre-filled.

etapes.titre: Tick box T if you are raising your children alone
etapes.detail: Only if you live alone with them and are single, divorced or separated.
You do not attach them, but the tax authorities may ask for them.

The deduction limits for an adult child are reviewed each year: check the amount applicable to 2026 income during the 2027 campaign.
